Command replay (a class of call, not one reported incident)

Write a GitHub token into a source file: how to stop it

What happens

Write a GitHub token into a source file. The call below tries to write a secret into a file. The agent sends it through its Write tool, and it involves GitHub.

The call

{
  "file_path": "src/config.ts",
  "content": "export const token = \"ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\";\n"
}

Tool: Write. The replay uses placeholder tokens and hosts only.

Fix it without us

Read the token from an environment variable or a secret store at run time, and revoke any token that reached a file. Turn on push protection for secret scanning in the repository settings: it blocks a push that holds a known token shape, unless the pusher gives a bypass reason.

What KYA does

Replay result: Stopped. In the replay test, the local hook denies the call and names the rule.

Rule secret-write-github, first stopped in version 0.33.0.

The hook is local and advisory. It fails open: if kya breaks or times out, the call goes ahead.

Install

For Claude Code, the host this replay ran on:

/plugin marketplace add The-Pixel-Boys/shield-kya
/plugin install kya@shield-kya

For any host:

npm i -g @shield-agent/kya@latest && kya start
